memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'From the fellowship offering you are to bring a food offering to the LORD: its fat, the entire fat tail cut off close to the backbone, the internal organs and all the fat that is connected to them, both kidneys with the fat on them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver, which you will remove with the kidneys.'" - Lev 3:9-10 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The fat tail deserves a word. The sheep of that region had large, heavy tails composed almost entirely of fat — sometimes weighing several kilos. It was considered a delicacy, the choicest eating on the animal.

And God asks for it. The whole tail, cut off close to the backbone so none of it is held back.

There is a phrase in older English translations used for the priests' portion: the fat of the land. It comes from this world of thinking, where fat meant the richest and most desirable part.

So the question this verse quietly puts to us is this: what is the fat tail in my life? What is the choicest thing, the part I would most want to keep for myself?

For one person it is money. For another it is time — the free evening, the untouched Saturday. For another it is talent, or reputation, or a relationship they hold too tightly.

God is not being greedy. He is being honest with us about the human heart. Jesus said it plainly: where your treasure is, there your heart will be also (Mtt 6:21). What we refuse to give God tends to be exactly what is ruling us.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. What is the "fat tail" I would least want to hand over to God?
2. Is there something I am holding that has quietly begun to hold me?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You know what I am gripping most tightly. Loosen my hands, and let the choicest part of my life be Yours. Amen.
